name: MonarchUptimeBar
title: UptimeBar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with pointerInput tap gestures for the segments; androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox with RichTooltip (a persistent rememberTooltipState and a custom PopupPositionProvider) for the details of a period
summary: A row of per-period status segments, usually one per day, with the details of a period one tap away and the overall uptime under it.
whenToUse: On a status page, a service tile or a monitor row, to show how a service did over the last days or hours, period by period.
whenNotToUse: For a trend of a measured value, use MonarchLineChart or MonarchSparkline; for the share of each state over the whole period, MonarchStackedProportionBar; for one current state, MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchUptimeBar(segments: List<MonarchUptimeBarSegment>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, overallUptime: Double? = null, showOverallUptime: Boolean = true, startLabel: String? = null, endLabel: String? = null, thresholds: MonarchUptimeBarThresholds = MonarchUptimeBarThresholds(), size: MonarchUptimeBarSize = MonarchUptimeBarSize.Md, showLegend: Boolean = false, uptimeDigits: Int = 2, activeIndex: Int? = null, onActiveIndexChange: ((Int?) -> Unit)? = null, summary: String? = null, labels: MonarchUptimeBarLabels = MonarchUptimeBarLabels(), onSegmentSelect: ((MonarchUptimeBarSegment) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchUptimeBarSegment(id: String, label: String, status: MonarchUptimeBarStatus? = null, uptime: Double? = null, details: List<MonarchUptimeBarDetail> = emptyList(), note: String? = null)
enum class MonarchUptimeBarStatus { Operational, Degraded, Partial, Down, Maintenance, NoData }

class MonarchUptimeBarLabels(statusNames: Map<MonarchUptimeBarStatus, String> = emptyMap(), uptime: String? = null, overall: ((String) -> String)? = null, legend: String? = null, periods: String? = null, open: String? = null, summary: ((Int, Map<MonarchUptimeBarStatus, Int>, String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: segments
options.description: The periods, oldest first. Each has an id, a label, and a status or an uptime (or neither, for no data), with optional details and a note.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the whole bar.

options.name: label
options.description: What is monitored, such as a service name: shown above the bar and the bar's spoken name ("Uptime" when null).

options.name: description
options.description: A short line under the label, such as "Last 30 days".

options.name: overallUptime
options.description: The overall uptime in percent. The mean of the measured periods when null.

options.name: showOverallUptime
options.description: Whether the overall uptime is written under the bar.

options.name: startLabel
options.description: Text under the oldest period, such as "30 days ago".

options.name: endLabel
options.description: Text under the newest period, such as "Today".

options.name: thresholds
options.description: The cut points for periods with an uptime but no status: at or above operational is operational, at or above degraded is degraded, below is down.

options.name: size
options.description: The height of the segments: Md 32dp for status pages, Sm 20dp for tiles and rows. The touch area is at least 48dp high either way.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Lists the names of the colors under the bar. With several bars on a screen, show it on one.

options.name: uptimeDigits
options.description: The decimal places of uptime percentages.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected period, used when onActiveIndexChange is set. Give several bars one state to inspect the same period on each. An index outside the periods is ignored.

options.name: onActiveIndexChange
options.description: Makes the inspection controlled: called with the period the user taps, or null when the details close.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the state names, "Uptime", the overall line, "Legend", "Periods", "Open" and the summary.

options.name: onSegmentSelect
options.description: Opens a period in the app, such as that day's incidents: from the Open button in the details, or from the period's TalkBack action.

states.name: default
states.description: Every segment in its state's color from the start edge, 2dp apart (1dp when segments get narrower than 4dp); no data is a muted, outlined segment.

states.name: inspected
states.description: The inspected segment has a 2dp ring in the default text color, set off by a hairline of the surface color.

states.name: details open
states.description: After a tap, a Material 3 rich tooltip over the segment shows the period as its title, the state with its marker, the uptime, the details and the note, and Open with onSegmentSelect. A tap outside closes it and clears the inspection.

states.name: empty
states.description: No periods: an empty touch area, and a summary of zero periods.

appearance: Operational periods use the success solid color, degraded the warning solid, partial outages the warning strong, down the danger solid and maintenance the info solid; no data is the muted background with a default border. The label is body text, the description, start and end labels muted caption text, and the overall line caption text in the default color. The details take the Material 3 rich tooltip colors of the Monarch theme. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Touch replaces hover: the web shows a tooltip while the pointer moves and keyboard arrows move through the days; here a tap opens the details in a Material 3 RichTooltip placed over the segment, and TalkBack users swipe through one element per period. Unlike iOS, where the bar is one adjustable element, Android follows the Monarch chart pattern of one image element with the summary followed by one element per period, because TalkBack has no adjustable role for custom views in Compose. The parameters start with segments, the only required one, as the Compose guidelines ask; iOS takes the label first. The web dims the other segments while one is inspected; here only the ring marks it, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. The web meta slot (a badge in the header) is not offered: put the bar in a Row with the badge. The web exports a separate UptimeLegend; here showLegend draws the same list. The web keeps a hidden data table and iOS a chart descriptor; Android has no chart descriptor, and each period element reads all of its details instead. The parity map named chart-frame as a dependency: the bar does not sit in a MonarchChartFrame card, as on the web and iOS, so it fits in tiles and rows; it has its own label line. Segments run from the start edge, so the oldest day is on the right in right to left.
accessibility: The bar is one element with the image role, named by label (or "Uptime"), whose state description is the summary, such as "Periods: 30. Operational 28, Degraded 1, Down 1. Uptime 99.86%". Only the states present are counted.

After it, one element per period in order (traversal index), placed over the period's segment and read as the period and its details, such as "Mar 2: Degraded, Uptime 99.42%, Checks 1,440, Slow responses".
With onSegmentSelect each period element has a custom action "Open, Mar 2"; without it, the elements have no action.
The touch area of the bar is at least 48dp high in both sizes.
Every state has a name in the details, the legend and the summary, so color never carries it alone; no data is drawn hollow.
The label above the bar and the start, end and overall line under it are hidden from TalkBack, because the bar's name and summary say them.
The legend is a traversal group named "Legend"; each entry is read as its state name.
edgeCases: A segment's own status wins over its uptime.
A segment with neither a status nor a finite uptime has no data.
The overall uptime averages only the measured segments; with none it is not shown.
With 90 segments each can be under 3dp wide; a tap still finds the segment under the finger from its position.
An activeIndex outside the segments is ignored.
Tapping outside the details closes them and clears the inspected segment; the details are not reachable with TalkBack, which reads the same text from each period element.
The tooltip and the touch inspection were checked with Robolectric tests, not on a device.

examples.title: Status page row
examples.template:
MonarchUptimeBar(
    segments = (1..{{days}}).map { day ->
            MonarchUptimeBarSegment(
                id = "${{{monthKey}}}-$day",
                label = "${{{month}}} $day",
                status = if (day == {{maintenanceDay}}) MonarchUptimeBarStatus.Maintenance else null,
                uptime = if (day == {{noDataDay}}) null else if (day == {{down.day}}) {{down.uptime}} else if (day == {{degraded.day}}) {{degraded.uptime}} else 100.0,
                details = if (day == {{noDataDay}}) emptyList() else listOf(MonarchUptimeBarDetail({{detailLabel}}, "${{{checks}}}")),
                note = if (day == {{down.day}}) {{down.note}} else null,
            )
        },
    label = {{label}},
    description = {{description}},
    startLabel = {{startLabel}},
    endLabel = {{endLabel}},
    showLegend = true,
)
examples.code:
MonarchUptimeBar(
    segments = (1..30).map { day ->
            MonarchUptimeBarSegment(
                id = "${"2026-03"}-$day",
                label = "${"Mar"} $day",
                status = if (day == 25) MonarchUptimeBarStatus.Maintenance else null,
                uptime = if (day == 1) null else if (day == 12) 97.8 else if (day == 20) 99.4 else 100.0,
                details = if (day == 1) emptyList() else listOf(MonarchUptimeBarDetail("Checks", "${1440}")),
                note = if (day == 12) "Elevated error rate" else null,
            )
        },
    label = "Public API",
    description = "api.example.com",
    startLabel = "30 days ago",
    endLabel = "Today",
    showLegend = true,
)

examples.title: Two small bars sharing one inspected day
examples.code:
Column {
    MonarchUptimeBar(
        segments = days,
        label = "API",
        size = MonarchUptimeBarSize.Sm,
        activeIndex = active,
        onActiveIndexChange = { active = it },
    )
    MonarchUptimeBar(
        segments = days,
        label = "Website",
        size = MonarchUptimeBarSize.Sm,
        activeIndex = active,
        onActiveIndexChange = { active = it },
    )
}

examples.title: Opening a day in the app
examples.code:
MonarchUptimeBar(
    segments = listOf(
        MonarchUptimeBarSegment("1", "Mar 1", uptime = 100.0),
        MonarchUptimeBarSegment(
            id = "2",
            label = "Mar 2",
            uptime = 99.42,
            details = listOf(MonarchUptimeBarDetail("Checks", "1,440")),
        ),
    ),
    label = "Search API",
    onSegmentSelect = { opened = it.id },
)
